chapter: New Orleans dance scene of the 1920s
title: Places where society dances were held
summary: Audubon Tea Room, Tulane Gym, the Quartier Club, the Sazerac Bar and fraternity dances, as distinct from cabarets; interviewer mentions a rough club behind chicken wire.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: And so, you might be interested in knowing some of the places that these dances were given, in addition to private homes, of course. Or places like the Audubon Tea Room, Tulane Gym, the Cartier Club. Have you heard of it? Never have.

I don't know. I have it, Q-U-A-R-T-I-E-R, that's what it sounds like. And I don't recall the exact spelling, but it was in the quarter, right around Jackson Square in that neighborhood. Never heard of it. Then there were dances given at the old Sazerac Bar, which was on Royal Street. I'll mention the Audubon Tea Room, of course. But there were many sororities and fraternities around town. And, you know, once you went to one of these dances, or several of them, you were almost automatically invited to others, and more or less the same group would be at these places.
The same kind of people being at the Cadillac that would be at the Audubon Tea Room?
Oh, no, no, I didn't mean that. No.
Well, I've tried to get a...

No, I meant the dances. I didn't... I wasn't referring to any clubs, nightclubs or cabarets. At that time, well, the youngsters didn't get around to those places too often. Money was scarce for one thing, and then... Wasn't quite the place to go for a lot of them.
Did Raymond ever tell you about that place? He never played there, but the band was behind Chicken Wire, so they wouldn't be hit by flying bottles. No, but I don't doubt it.
No, but I don't doubt it.
On Galliope Street. I don't doubt it.
